Leave out the red onion and Dijon, use fully set eggs and serve it cool rather than cold.
Add a second egg half to each bowl.
faq: Which tuna should I use?
Light tuna in water, drained, is what the nutrition estimate is based on. Brands vary, so check the label.
Can I make it ahead?
Yes. The salad keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Add the greens and eggs just before serving.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, as written. Check your mustard label if you are very sensitive.
note: This is the salad for days when cooking sounds like too much. Everything except the eggs comes from a can or the crisper drawer, and a small bowl still covers a good share of the day's protein.

title: Baked Cinnamon Apples with Greek Yogurt
subtitle: Small apples filled with oats, walnuts and dried cranberries, baked until soft and served warm with a spoonful of vanilla Greek yogurt.
desc: Soft baked apples with a spoonful of yogurt.
intro: Baked apples are soft, warm and gently sweet, the kind of dessert that is easy to eat in small spoonfuls. Each small apple is filled with oats, walnuts and dried cranberries, baked until tender and served with a spoonful of vanilla Greek yogurt for about 8 g of protein.

Coring the apples while leaving the bottoms intact turns each one into a little cup that holds the filling and catches the juices. A splash of water in the dish creates steam, which softens the apples evenly before the tops start to brown. Baking until a knife slides in with no resistance gives a texture closer to apple sauce than crisp fruit.
why: Fork-tender apples that are easy to eat in small spoonfuls.
A spoonful of vanilla Greek yogurt on each apple.
Bake a pan, then warm one apple at a time during the week.

items.note: such as Gala or Honeycrisp, about 5 oz / 150 g each

steps.d: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and choose a small baking dish that holds the four apples snugly.
Use a melon baller or small spoon to scoop the core out of each apple from the top, leaving about 1/2 inch at the bottom so the filling stays in. Widen the opening to about 1 1/2 inches.
steps.tip: If an apple wobbles, slice a thin piece off the bottom so it sits flat.

steps.d: In a small bowl, stir together the oats, walnuts, cranberries, melted butter, maple syrup, cinnamon and salt until the oats are evenly coated.

Set the apples in the dish and pack the filling into each one, mounding any extra on top. Pour the water into the dish, cover loosely with foil and bake for 20 minutes. Uncover and bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until a knife slides into the side of an apple with no resistance and the tops are golden.
steps.tip: Covering for the first part of baking steams the apples so they soften all the way through before the filling browns.

steps.d: Stir the vanilla into the yogurt. Let the apples cool for 5 minutes, spoon a little of the pan juices over each one and serve with a spoonful of the yogurt and a pinch of cinnamon.

tips: Choose apples that hold their shape when baked, such as Gala, Honeycrisp or Braeburn. Very soft varieties can collapse.
Smaller apples cook faster and make a better single portion than large ones.
Spoon the pan juices back over the apples before serving; that is where much of the flavor ends up.
Small-portion tip: serve half an apple with a spoonful of yogurt. Cover the other half and warm it later.
storage: Refrigerate cooled apples in an airtight container for up to 4 days, with the yogurt kept separately. Reheat in the microwave for 45 to 60 seconds, or in a 350°F (175°C) oven for about 10 minutes, until warm through.
variations: Use small ripe but firm pears, halved and cored, and bake cut side up for 20 to 25 minutes.
Replace the walnuts with pumpkin seeds.
Use coconut oil instead of butter and serve with a thick plant yogurt.
Peel the apples before baking and skip the walnuts for a softer, smoother texture.
Serve with a larger spoonful of Greek yogurt, or stir a little vanilla protein powder into the yogurt.
faq: Do I need to peel the apples?
No. The skin helps the apples keep their shape. Peel them if you prefer a softer texture, and expect them to cook a few minutes faster.
How do I know when they are done?
A thin knife should slide into the side of the apple with no resistance, and the skin will look slightly wrinkled.
Can I make them gluten-free?
Yes. Use oats labeled certified gluten-free.
note: Warm, soft and gently sweet, this is the kind of dessert that does not ask much of a small appetite. A spoonful of yogurt on top turns it into something closer to a small meal. Bake the whole pan; the leftovers reheat well.

title: Greek Yogurt Berry Parfait Jars
subtitle: Layers of vanilla Greek yogurt, fresh strawberries, blueberries and a little granola in small jars. About 20 g protein each, ready in the fridge for the week.
desc: Cold, creamy and ready when you are.
intro: A parfait is one of the easiest ways to get protein in before the day gets busy. Thick Greek yogurt does most of the work, with about 20 g of protein in each small jar, and fresh berries keep it bright and light.
The trick for make-ahead jars is keeping the granola crisp. A spoonful goes on top just before eating, or in a small separate container, so the layers stay creamy and the crunch stays crunchy.
why: Most of it comes from thick Greek yogurt.
Ten minutes of layering covers four breakfasts.
Easy on mornings when warm food does not appeal.

steps.d: Stir the Greek yogurt, honey and vanilla together in a bowl until smooth.
Spoon a layer of yogurt into four small jars or glasses (about 8 oz each). Add a layer of berries and a pinch of chia seeds, then repeat, finishing with berries on top.
steps.tip: Small jars help: a full jar you can finish beats a big bowl you cannot.

steps.d: Cover and refrigerate for up to 4 days.
Just before eating, scatter about 2 tablespoons of granola over each jar.

tips: Pat the berries dry after washing so the yogurt does not turn watery.
Frozen berries work too. Layer them frozen and they thaw in the fridge overnight.
Keep the granola in a small separate container if you are packing a jar to go.
Small-portion tip: eat half a jar now and put the lid back on. It keeps well for later.
storage: Refrigerate the covered jars, without granola, for up to 4 days. Do not freeze.
variations: Use diced peaches and a pinch of cinnamon instead of the berries.
Stir 1 tablespoon cocoa powder into the yogurt with a little extra honey.
Skip the granola and chia, and use soft berries like ripe strawberries or mashed raspberries.
Stir 2 tablespoons vanilla protein powder into the yogurt, loosening with a splash of milk.
faq: Can I use flavored yogurt?
Yes, but most flavored yogurts have more sugar and less protein. Plain Greek yogurt with a little honey gives you more control.
Why add the granola last?
Granola softens in yogurt within a few hours. Adding it at the end keeps the crunch.
Is it dairy-free?
Not as written. A thick coconut or soy yogurt works, though the protein will be lower.
note: Four jars on Sunday means four mornings where breakfast is already done. Cold, creamy and easy to stop halfway.

title: Smoked Salmon Bagel Halves
subtitle: Half an everything bagel with a whipped cream cheese and Greek yogurt spread, smoked salmon, cucumber and dill. About 16 g protein per half, no cooking.
desc: A deli breakfast in a smaller portion.
intro: A whole bagel with lox is a lot of food. Served open-faced as halves, it becomes a breakfast you can actually finish, with about 16 g of protein in each half from the smoked salmon and a lighter spread.
The spread is half light cream cheese and half Greek yogurt, whipped with lemon and dill. It tastes like the deli version but adds protein and spreads more easily, so a thin layer is enough.
why: Smoked salmon and a Greek yogurt spread.
One half is a small plate. Two make a bigger one.

steps.d: Stir the cream cheese, Greek yogurt, lemon juice and dill together until smooth and fluffy.
Toast the bagel halves until lightly golden. Let them cool for a minute so the spread does not melt.
Spread a thin layer of the cream cheese mixture over each half. Top with cucumber slices and fold the smoked salmon over the top.
steps.tip: Cucumber under the salmon keeps the bagel from turning soggy if you pack it to go.

steps.d: Scatter with capers, extra dill and black pepper, and serve with lemon wedges.

tips: Scoop out a little of the soft bagel center for an even lighter base.
Smoked salmon is salty, so taste before adding capers.
The spread keeps for 4 days, so make a double batch.

Small-portion tip: one prepared bagel half is the standard serving here, with about 16 g protein. For a smaller plate, eat half of that bagel half, with the spread and salmon shared the same way, for about 8 g. Cut it into quarters to eat slowly.
storage: Best assembled fresh. Refrigerate the spread for up to 4 days and opened smoked salmon according to the package, usually 3 to 5 days.
variations: Add a sliced hard-boiled egg for about 6 g more protein.
Swap the cucumber for thin slices of avocado.
Use a gluten-free bagel or a slice of gluten-free toast.
Skip the capers and pepper, use a plain bagel and choose a mild, lightly smoked salmon.
Use 2 ounces of salmon per half instead of 1.5.
faq: Is smoked salmon cooked?
Cold-smoked salmon is cured, not cooked. If you have been advised to avoid it, use hot-smoked or canned salmon.
Can I make it the night before?
Make the spread ahead, but assemble the bagels the same day so they stay crisp.
Which bagel works best?
Any you like. Everything, sesame and plain are classic. Mini bagels make an even smaller portion.
note: This is the weekend brunch plate made small enough for a weekday. One half, a cup of tea, done.

title: Cottage Cheese Scrambled Eggs
subtitle: Soft, creamy scrambled eggs with cottage cheese stirred in, served with a slice of toast, a little avocado and greens. About 24 g protein per plate.
desc: The creamiest eggs, with extra protein.
intro: Cottage cheese is the quiet trick behind some of the creamiest scrambled eggs you can make. It melts into the eggs as they cook, adding about 6 g of protein per plate and a soft, custardy texture without any cream.
Low heat matters more than anything here. Eggs cooked slowly stay tender and moist, which makes them easier to eat on days when chewing feels like effort.
why: Low heat keeps the curds tender.

items.n: salt, black pepper and chopped chives

steps.d: Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt until no streaks of white remain. Stir in the cottage cheese.
Melt the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the eggs and let them sit for 20 seconds, then push them gently across the pan with a spatula, forming large soft curds.
steps.tip: If the eggs start to set too fast, lift the pan off the heat for a few seconds.

steps.d: When the eggs are mostly set but still glossy, about 2 to 3 minutes, take the pan off the heat. They finish cooking from the warmth of the pan.
Serve the eggs with toast, sliced avocado and greens. Finish with black pepper and chives.

tips: Small-curd cottage cheese melts in most smoothly.
Salt the eggs before cooking; cottage cheese is already salty, so go lightly.
A nonstick pan makes low-heat scrambling much easier.
Small-portion tip: start with the eggs and add the toast only if you still want it.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Leftovers keep for 1 day in the fridge; reheat gently in the microwave in 15-second bursts.
variations: Wilt a handful of spinach in the pan before adding the eggs.
Stir in chopped dill or parsley at the end.
Serve with gluten-free toast or roasted potatoes.
Skip the pepper and chives, cook the eggs very soft and serve them without the toast.
Add one more egg, or top with a spoonful of extra cottage cheese.
faq: Will I see the cottage cheese?
A few soft curds, but it mostly melts into the eggs.
Can I blend the cottage cheese first?
Yes. Blending it with the eggs gives an even smoother scramble.
Can I make it for one?
Yes. Halve everything and use a small pan.
note: Soft eggs are one of the gentlest breakfasts there is. The cottage cheese just makes them work a little harder for you.

title: Berry Greek Yogurt Muffins
subtitle: Soft, small berry muffins made with Greek yogurt and a scoop of vanilla protein powder. About 7 g protein each, and they freeze well.
desc: A small, soft muffin with a little extra protein.
intro: Bakery muffins are often the size of a small cake. These are regular-size, soft and lightly sweet, and Greek yogurt plus a little vanilla protein powder gives each one about 7 g of protein.
They are made for the freezer. Bake a batch, freeze them individually, and warm one for 20 seconds when you want something small with a cup of coffee.
why: Greek yogurt, eggs and protein powder.
Warm one at a time from frozen.
Easy to eat in a few small bites.

items.note: raspberries and blueberries, fresh or frozen

steps.d: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line or grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Whisk the flour, protein powder, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the yogurt, eggs, maple syrup, oil, milk and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and fold with a spatula until just combined. Fold in the berries.
steps.tip: Stop as soon as no dry flour remains. Overmixing makes protein muffins tough.

steps.d: Divide the batter among the cups and bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the tops spring back and a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then on a rack.

tips: If using frozen berries, add them straight from the freezer so they do not bleed into the batter.
Protein powders vary a lot. If your batter is very thick, add another tablespoon of milk.
Check them at 17 minutes; protein muffins can dry out if overbaked.
Small-portion tip: half a muffin on its own has about 3 to 4 g protein. With 1 cup milk (about 8 g) the snack comes to about 11 to 12 g.
For a breakfast with more protein, pair one muffin with 1/2 cup plain nonfat Greek yogurt for about 18 g protein in total.
storage: Keep at room temperature for 1 day, in the fridge for up to 4 days, or freeze individually for up to 3 months. Warm from frozen in the microwave for 20 to 30 seconds.
variations: Add the zest of one lemon to the wet ingredients.
Use 1 1/2 cups flour in total. Each muffin will have about 5 g protein.
Replace the maple syrup with 1/2 cup mashed ripe banana and add 1 tablespoon sugar.
Use blueberries only and skip any crunchy topping. Serve slightly warm.
Serve with a spoonful of Greek yogurt or a glass of milk.
faq: Can I use plant-based protein powder?
Yes, but it absorbs more liquid. Add milk a tablespoon at a time until the batter is thick but scoopable.
Why are my muffins dry?
Usually overbaking or overmixing. Pull them as soon as a toothpick comes out clean.
Can I make mini muffins?
Yes. Bake in a mini tin for 10 to 12 minutes.
note: A muffin is often the only thing that sounds good with morning coffee. These are smaller, softer and do a little more for you.

title: Strawberry Cottage Cheese Bowl
subtitle: Creamy cottage cheese with fresh strawberries, a drizzle of honey and a few toasted almonds. About 26 g protein in five minutes.
desc: Five minutes, 26 g of protein.
intro: Some breakfasts are barely a recipe, and this is one of them. A cup of cottage cheese, a handful of ripe strawberries and a drizzle of honey add up to about 26 g of protein with no cooking at all.
Cottage cheese has had a comeback for good reason: it is mild, cool and soft, which makes it easy to eat on low-appetite days. The berries add sweetness, and a few almonds add a little crunch.
why: Almost all of it from cottage cheese.
A gentle choice when warm food does not appeal.

steps.d: Toast the almonds in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until golden. Let them cool.
steps.tip: Toast a whole bag at once and keep it in a jar for the week.

steps.d: Slice the strawberries. If they are not very sweet, toss them with half the honey and let them sit for 5 minutes.
Divide the cottage cheese between two bowls or plates. Top with the strawberries, drizzle with the remaining honey and scatter over the almonds and mint.

tips: Whipped cottage cheese, blended for 30 seconds, gives a smoother, yogurt-like texture.
Ripe, in-season strawberries need little or no honey.
Frozen strawberries, thawed, release juice that makes a nice quick sauce.
Small-portion tip: make half a bowl, halving the cottage cheese and every topping. That half has about 13 g protein.
storage: Best fresh. Sliced strawberries keep for 2 days in the fridge; assemble the bowls when you are ready to eat.
variations: Use sliced peaches and a pinch of cinnamon.
Skip the fruit and honey; top with cherry tomatoes, cucumber, olive oil and pepper.
Use toasted pumpkin seeds or granola instead of almonds.
Blend the cottage cheese smooth, skip the almonds and use very ripe, soft berries.
Stir in 2 tablespoons of hemp seeds or add a spoonful of Greek yogurt.
faq: I do not like the texture of cottage cheese. Any tips?
Blend it for 30 seconds. It turns completely smooth, like thick yogurt.
Which cottage cheese is best?
Small-curd 2% is creamy and mild. Check labels, since sodium and protein vary between brands.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, as written.
note: On mornings when cooking feels like too much, this is the five-minute answer. Spoon it onto a plate and you are done.

title: Strawberry Greek Yogurt Smoothie
subtitle: Frozen strawberries blended with Greek yogurt and milk into a thick, cold smoothie. About 16 g protein per small glass, no protein powder needed.
desc: Thick, cold and about 16 g protein a glass.
intro: On days when chewing feels like work, a smoothie is often the easiest way to get some protein in. This one uses Greek yogurt instead of protein powder, so it tastes like strawberries and cream rather than a supplement, with about 16 g of protein in each small glass.
Frozen strawberries do two jobs: they make the smoothie cold and thick without ice, and they keep well in the freezer so you can make a glass whenever you want one.
why: From Greek yogurt and milk, no powder.
Everything goes straight into the blender.
A small glass you can finish over half an hour.

steps.d: Pour the milk into the blender, then add the yogurt, honey and vanilla.
steps.tip: Liquid at the bottom helps the blades move and keeps the blender from stalling.

steps.d: Add the frozen strawberries on top.
Blend on low for a few seconds, then on high for 45 to 60 seconds, until completely smooth. Add a splash more milk if it is too thick to pour.
Pour into two small glasses. Drink one now and keep the other covered in the fridge for later in the day.

tips: Taste before adding honey; ripe frozen strawberries are often sweet enough.
For a thicker, spoonable smoothie, use 3/4 cup milk.
Fresh strawberries work too; add a few ice cubes for chill.
Small-portion tip: sip it slowly over 20 to 30 minutes. It does not need to be finished in one go.
storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate a covered glass for up to 24 hours and shake or stir before drinking. Freeze leftovers in ice pop molds for up to 1 month.
variations: Replace 1 cup of strawberries with half a frozen banana.
Use a soy yogurt and soy milk; the protein will be a little lower.
Blend in 2 tablespoons rolled oats for a more filling glass.
Use a mild, plain yogurt, skip the honey and let it sit for a few minutes so it is cool rather than icy.
Blend in one scoop of vanilla protein powder for about 12 g more protein per glass.
faq: Can I make it ahead?
Yes, up to a day. It separates a little; shake or stir it before drinking.
Do I need a high-powered blender?
No. Add the milk first and blend in short bursts if your blender struggles.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, as written.
note: When a plate of food feels like too much, a small glass often does not. Keep a bag of frozen strawberries in the freezer for exactly those days.

title: Banana Vanilla Protein Smoothie
subtitle: A creamy banana smoothie with Greek yogurt, milk, vanilla and a pinch of cinnamon. Tastes like a milkshake, with about 16 g protein per small glass.
desc: A milkshake-style smoothie with real protein.
intro: A frozen banana blends into something that tastes surprisingly close to a vanilla milkshake. Add Greek yogurt and milk and each small glass has about 16 g of protein, with nothing more than a pinch of cinnamon for flavor.
Bananas are also one of the mildest fruits there is, which makes this a good choice on days when strong flavors or acidic fruit do not sit well.
why: Greek yogurt and milk do the work.
Banana, vanilla and a little cinnamon.

steps.d: Peel a ripe banana, slice it and freeze the slices on a plate or in a bag for at least 2 hours.
steps.tip: Freeze several bananas at once. Spotty, very ripe bananas make the sweetest smoothies.

steps.d: Add the milk, yogurt, vanilla and cinnamon to the blender, then the frozen banana. Blend until smooth and thick, about 45 seconds.
Add ice for a colder, frothier smoothie, or a splash of milk if it is too thick.
Pour into two small glasses and dust with a little more cinnamon.

tips: No frozen banana? Use a fresh one and add 4 or 5 ice cubes.
The riper the banana, the sweeter and less starchy the smoothie.
Vanilla Greek yogurt works too; skip the vanilla extract.
Small-portion tip: one small glass is a full snack. Save the second for the afternoon.
storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate a covered glass for up to 12 hours; banana smoothies darken a little as they sit, which is harmless. Stir before drinking.
variations: Blend in 1 tablespoon peanut butter for extra flavor and about 2 g more protein per glass.
Replace half the milk with cold brewed coffee.
Use soy yogurt and soy milk.
Skip the cinnamon and ice, and use a very ripe banana for the softest flavor.
Add a scoop of vanilla protein powder and a splash more milk for about 12 g more protein per glass.
faq: Why freeze the banana?
It makes the smoothie thick and cold without watering it down with lots of ice.
Can I use a green banana?
It works, but it tastes starchy and less sweet. Ripe is best.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, as written.
note: This is the smoothie for days when nothing sounds good. Mild, sweet, cold, and easy to sip slowly.

title: Mixed Berry Protein Smoothie
subtitle: Frozen mixed berries, Greek yogurt, milk and a spoonful of chia blended into a thick, deep-purple smoothie. About 16 g protein and 5 g fiber per small glass.
desc: Bright berries, 16 g protein, 5 g fiber.
intro: A bag of frozen mixed berries is one of the most useful things to keep in the freezer. Blended with Greek yogurt and milk, it makes a thick, bright smoothie with about 16 g of protein in each small glass.
A spoonful of chia seeds adds fiber and makes the smoothie a little thicker as it sits, which is helpful when you want something that feels more like a small meal.
why: Ready any day of the week.

items.n: a few fresh berries or edible flowers

steps.d: Add the milk, yogurt, chia seeds and honey to the blender, then the frozen berries.
Blend on high for about 60 seconds, until completely smooth and no chia specks remain whole.
steps.tip: If you prefer a smoother texture, soak the chia in the milk for 5 minutes before blending.

steps.d: Add milk a tablespoon at a time if the smoothie is too thick to sip through a straw.
Pour into two small glasses and top with a few fresh berries if you like.

tips: Mixed berries vary in tartness; taste and add honey only if needed.
Raspberries and blackberries have seeds. Strain through a sieve for a seed-free smoothie.
The smoothie thickens as it sits because of the chia. Stir in a splash of milk before drinking.
Small-portion tip: a small glass now and the rest later counts just as much.
storage: Refrigerate a covered glass for up to 24 hours. It will thicken; stir in a little milk before drinking.
variations: Use all blueberries for a milder, sweeter smoothie.
Blend in a small handful of baby spinach; the berries hide the color and flavor.
Use soy yogurt and soy milk.
Use blueberries and strawberries only, skip the chia and strain out any seeds.
Blend in a scoop of unflavored or vanilla protein powder for about 12 g more protein per glass.
faq: Fresh or frozen berries?
Frozen give the best thick, cold texture. With fresh berries, add a handful of ice.
Can I skip the chia?
Yes. The smoothie will be a little thinner, with about 2 g less fiber per glass.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, as written.
note: Bright, cold and a little tart. On slow mornings, one small glass of this is an easy way to start the day.

title: Golden Milk Turmeric Latte
subtitle: Warm or iced milk gently spiced with turmeric, cinnamon and ginger. Made with ultra-filtered milk for about 13 g protein per glass.
desc: A soothing spiced milk with real protein.
intro: Golden milk is warm milk spiced with turmeric, cinnamon and ginger. It is soothing, lightly sweet and easy to sip slowly, which makes it a good evening drink or a gentle start to the day.
Using ultra-filtered milk, the kind sold with higher protein on the label, gives each glass about 13 g of protein without changing the taste. Regular milk works too, with about 8 g per glass.
why: Sip it hot in winter or over ice in summer.
Turmeric, cinnamon and a little ginger.

steps.d: Add the milk, turmeric, cinnamon, ginger and pepper to a small saucepan and whisk until no lumps remain.
Heat over medium-low, whisking often, until steaming but not boiling, about 4 to 5 minutes.
steps.tip: Do not let it boil. Ultra-filtered milk can catch on the bottom of the pan if the heat is too high.

steps.d: Take the pan off the heat and stir in the honey and vanilla. Taste and adjust.
Pour into two glasses or mugs. For iced golden milk, let it cool, then pour over ice.

tips: Turmeric stains. Rinse the pan and whisk right away.
Whisking or frothing the milk before serving gives it a latte-style foam.
A pinch of black pepper is traditional; leave it out if you prefer.
Small-portion tip: start with half a glass. Keep the rest in the fridge and warm it later.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered jar for up to 3 days. Shake well, then warm gently or serve over ice.
variations: Use soy milk for the most protein among plant milks.
Add a pinch of cardamom and a small pinch of cloves.
Use 1 teaspoon each grated fresh turmeric and ginger, then strain.
Halve the turmeric, skip the pepper and ginger, and serve it warm rather than hot.
Whisk in a scoop of unflavored collagen or vanilla protein powder off the heat.
faq: What is ultra-filtered milk?
Milk filtered to concentrate the protein and reduce the sugar. Check labels; most have around 13 g protein per cup.
Does it contain caffeine?
No. That makes it a good evening drink.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, as written.
note: A warm glass of golden milk is one of the gentlest ways to end the day. Made with ultra-filtered milk, it is mild, lightly sweet and easy to sip slowly.

title: Ginger Egg Drop Soup
subtitle: Hot chicken bone broth with fresh ginger and silky ribbons of egg, ready in 15 minutes. About 16 g protein per mug, easy to sip on hard days.
desc: Silky egg ribbons in a gingery broth.
intro: Egg drop soup is one of the fastest soups there is: hot broth, a little cornstarch to give it body, and beaten eggs poured in slowly so they turn into soft, silky ribbons. It is light, warm and easy to sip from a mug.
Using chicken bone broth instead of regular stock adds a surprising amount of protein. With the eggs, each mug has about 16 g, and fresh ginger keeps it bright and soothing.

steps.d: Bring the broth, ginger and soy sauce to a simmer in a saucepan and simmer for 5 minutes. Remove the ginger slices if you used them.
Stir the cornstarch slurry, then whisk it into the simmering broth. Cook for 1 minute, until the broth turns slightly glossy.
Beat the eggs in a jug or bowl until completely smooth.
Stir the broth in a slow circle with one hand while you pour the eggs in a thin stream with the other. Stop stirring and let the soup sit for 30 seconds, until the ribbons set.
steps.tip: A slow, thin stream gives fine, silky ribbons. Pouring fast gives larger, fluffier pieces. Both are good.

steps.d: Turn off the heat, stir in the sesame oil and season with white pepper. Ladle into mugs or small bowls and scatter with scallions.

tips: Bone broth brands vary a lot in protein. Check the label; most have 8 to 10 g per cup.
Taste before adding more soy sauce; broth is often salty enough.
For the softest ribbons, keep the broth at a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil.
Small-portion tip: a single mug is an easy small meal. Reheat the rest one mug at a time.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stove or in the microwave; the ribbons stay soft. Not ideal for freezing, as the eggs turn spongy.
variations: Add 1/2 cup diced soft tofu with the eggs for about 3 g more protein per mug.
Stir in a handful of baby spinach just before the eggs.
Add 1/2 cup sweet corn for a classic egg drop and corn soup.
Skip the white pepper and scallions, use less ginger and let it cool to warm before sipping.
Stir in 1/2 cup shredded cooked chicken per mug.
faq: Is it gluten-free?
Use tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce and check that your broth is gluten-free.
Can I use regular chicken broth?
Yes, but the protein will drop to about 8 g per mug.
Why add cornstarch?
It gives the broth a little body so the egg ribbons stay suspended.
note: This is the soup to make when you are tired, cold or not very hungry. Ten minutes on the stove, then a warm mug to sip slowly.

title: Greek Yogurt Deviled Eggs with Crispy Bacon
subtitle: Classic deviled eggs made lighter with Greek yogurt and topped with a little crispy bacon. Three halves make a small snack with about 13 g protein.
desc: Creamy, savory and about 13 g protein.
intro: Deviled eggs are one of the most useful snacks to keep in the fridge: small, savory, already portioned and full of protein. This version swaps most of the mayonnaise for Greek yogurt, so the filling stays creamy and tangy with a little less fat.
Two slices of bacon go a long way here. Crumbled over the top, they add a salty crunch that makes three halves feel like a proper snack.
why: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

steps.d: Lower the eggs into a pot of gently boiling water and cook for 12 minutes. Move them straight into a bowl of ice water for 5 minutes.
steps.tip: Older eggs peel more easily than very fresh ones.

steps.d: Peel the eggs, cut them in half lengthwise and pop the yolks into a bowl. Arrange the whites on a plate.
Mash the yolks with a fork, then stir in the yogurt, mayonnaise and mustard until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon or pipe the filling back into the whites.
Scatter with crumbled bacon, chives and a pinch of paprika just before serving.

tips: A zip-top bag with one corner snipped off makes an easy piping bag.
Add the bacon just before serving so it stays crisp.
For the smoothest filling, press the yolks through a sieve.
Small-portion tip: plate three halves and keep the rest covered in the fridge for later.
storage: Refrigerate filled eggs in a covered container for up to 2 days. Keep the bacon separate and add it before eating. Not suitable for freezing.
variations: Top with smoked paprika and chives for a vegetarian version.
Mash 1/4 avocado into the filling for extra creaminess.
Top each half with a small piece of smoked salmon instead of bacon.
Skip the mustard, paprika and bacon and season the filling with just a little salt.
Serve with a small cup of cottage cheese or a few slices of turkey for about 8 g more protein.
faq: Can I make them ahead?
Yes. Make the filling and cook the eggs up to 2 days ahead; fill on the day for the neatest look.
Can I skip the mayonnaise?
Yes. Use 1/3 cup Greek yogurt in total; the filling will be a little tangier.
Are they gluten-free?
Yes, as long as your bacon and mustard are gluten-free.
note: Keep a few of these in the fridge for the moments when you know you should eat something but nothing sounds good.

title: Warm Garlic Sesame Edamame
subtitle: Steamed edamame tossed with sesame oil, a little garlic and flaky salt. Ready in 10 minutes, with about 14 g protein and 6 g fiber per bowl.
desc: A warm, salty bowl with real protein.
intro: A bag of frozen edamame is one of the easiest high-protein snacks there is. Steam the pods, toss them with a little sesame oil and garlic, sprinkle with salt and eat them warm, one pod at a time.
Popping the beans out of the pods slows you down, which is often helpful when your appetite is small. Each bowl has about 14 g of plant protein.

steps.d: Bring an inch of water to a boil in a pot with a steamer basket, or use a pot of boiling salted water. Cook the edamame for 5 to 6 minutes, until hot and tender. Drain well.
In the same pot, warm the sesame oil and garlic over low heat for 30 seconds, just until fragrant.
steps.tip: Keep the heat low; garlic turns bitter if it browns.

steps.d: Add the edamame and tamari and toss to coat.
Tip into two small bowls and sprinkle with flaky salt and sesame seeds. Squeeze the beans out of the pods with your teeth and discard the pods.

tips: Microwave option: cook the pods in a covered bowl with 2 tablespoons water for 4 to 5 minutes.
Shelled edamame works too; toss and eat with a spoon.
Put out a small empty bowl for the pods.
Small-portion tip: one bowl is a full snack. The second keeps well in the fridge and is good cold.
storage: Refrigerate cooked edamame in a covered container for up to 3 days. Eat cold or rewarm briefly in the microwave.
variations: Toss with lime zest and a pinch of chili flakes instead of garlic.
Skip the garlic and tamari; just salt.
Use shelled edamame and add diced cucumber for a quick salad.
Use shelled edamame, skip the garlic and season with a little salt only.
Serve alongside a soft-boiled egg for about 6 g more protein.
faq: Do you eat the pods?
No. The pods are tough; squeeze the beans out and discard the shells.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, with tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce.
Fresh or frozen?
Frozen is easier to find and already blanched, so it cooks faster.
note: A warm bowl of edamame is a good snack for slow afternoons. It takes ten minutes, and eating it pod by pod is almost relaxing.

title: Greek Yogurt Hummus with Spiced Chickpeas
subtitle: Extra-creamy hummus blended with Greek yogurt, topped with warm spiced chickpeas and herbs. About 9 g protein per small bowl, great with vegetables.
desc: Extra-creamy hummus with a protein lift.
intro: Blending a little Greek yogurt into hummus makes it extra smooth and adds a bit more protein, while keeping the familiar flavor of chickpeas, tahini and lemon.
A handful of chickpeas warmed in olive oil with paprika and cumin goes on top. Serve a small bowl with vegetables or a few crackers for a snack that keeps well in the fridge all week.

steps.d: Set aside 1/3 cup of the drained chickpeas for the topping.

Blend the remaining chickpeas with the yogurt, tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt for 2 minutes, scraping down the sides, until very smooth. Add a tablespoon or two of the reserved chickpea liquid if it is too thick.
steps.tip: Blending longer than you think makes the smoothest hummus.

steps.d: Warm the olive oil in a small skillet over medium heat. Add the saved chickpeas, paprika and cumin and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until lightly crisp.
Spread the hummus in a bowl, spoon the warm chickpeas and their oil on top and scatter with herbs.

tips: Taste and add more lemon or salt after blending.
Serve with cucumber, carrots, bell pepper or a few whole-grain crackers.
For a dairy-free version, use 1/4 cup extra chickpea liquid instead of yogurt.
Small-portion tip: spoon 1/3 cup into a small bowl rather than eating from the big one.
storage: Refrigerate the hummus in a covered container for up to 5 days. Store the topping separately and rewarm briefly before serving.
variations: Blend in 1/2 cup jarred roasted red peppers.
Blend in a handful of parsley and extra lemon zest.
Replace the yogurt with chickpea liquid and a little more tahini.
Skip the garlic, paprika and cumin and serve with soft cucumber slices.
Serve with a hard-boiled egg or a few slices of chicken for about 6 to 8 g more protein.
faq: Do I need to peel the chickpeas?
No. Blending for 2 minutes gives a smooth result without peeling.
Can I use dried chickpeas?
Yes, about 1 1/2 cups cooked chickpeas replaces one can.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes. Choose gluten-free crackers if serving with crackers.
note: A small bowl of hummus and some crunchy vegetables is one of the easiest snacks to put together when you are tired.

title: Greek Yogurt Tzatziki with Crunchy Vegetables
subtitle: Thick Greek yogurt with grated cucumber, dill, mint and lemon, served with fresh vegetables. A cool, refreshing snack with about 10 g protein per serving.
desc: Cool, creamy and about 10 g protein.
intro: Tzatziki is mostly Greek yogurt, which makes it one of the few dips that is genuinely high in protein. Grated cucumber, dill, mint and lemon keep it cool and fresh, and it takes ten minutes with no cooking.
Served cold with crunchy vegetables, it is a good snack for warm days or for when hot food does not appeal.

steps.d: Grate the cucumber on the coarse side of a box grater. Wrap it in a clean towel and squeeze out as much liquid as you can.
steps.tip: Squeezing the cucumber keeps the tzatziki thick instead of watery.

steps.d: Stir the yogurt, cucumber, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, dill, mint and salt together in a bowl.
If you have time, chill for 15 minutes so the flavors come together.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with a little more olive oil and serve with the vegetables.

tips: Use full-fat Greek yogurt for an even creamier dip; the protein stays about the same.
Tzatziki also works as a sauce for chicken, salmon or meatballs.
Grate the garlic finely so it blends in.
Small-portion tip: about 1/3 cup with a handful of vegetables is one serving.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 4 days. Stir before serving; a little liquid may collect on top. Store the cut vegetables separately.
variations: Skip the mint and add lemon zest.
Use parsley or chives instead of dill and mint.
Serve with warm pita triangles instead of vegetables.
Skip the garlic and serve with soft peeled cucumber slices.
Serve with a few slices of grilled chicken for about 10 g more protein.
faq: Why is my tzatziki watery?
The cucumber was not squeezed enough. Pour off any liquid and stir.
Can I use regular yogurt?
Strain it in a coffee filter for an hour first, or the dip will be thin and lower in protein.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, served with vegetables.
note: On days when everything feels too heavy, a cold bowl of tzatziki and crunchy vegetables often still sounds good.

title: Frozen Greek Yogurt Berry Bars
subtitle: Creamy Greek yogurt sweetened with a little honey, topped with raspberries and blackberries and frozen into small bars. About 6 g protein each.
desc: A cold, creamy bite with real protein.
intro: These bars taste like frozen yogurt, cut into small squares. Greek yogurt sweetened with a little honey is spread in a pan, topped with berries and frozen until firm.
Each bar has about 6 g of protein and only around 70 calories, which makes them a good cold treat for warm days or when you want something small and sweet.
why: Good on hot or queasy days.

steps.d: Line an 8 x 4-inch loaf pan with parchment paper, leaving some hanging over the sides.
Stir the yogurt, honey and vanilla together until smooth.
Spread the yogurt evenly in the pan. Press the berries gently into the top.
Freeze uncovered for at least 4 hours, until firm.
steps.tip: A loaf pan makes thicker, creamier bars than a baking sheet.

steps.d: Lift the block out using the parchment, let it sit for 5 minutes, then cut into 8 bars with a warm knife.

tips: Halve large blackberries so they sit flat.
Let a bar sit at room temperature for 5 minutes before eating for a softer bite.
Vanilla Greek yogurt works; skip the honey.
Small-portion tip: one bar is a full treat. Keep the rest in the freezer.
storage: Freeze the cut bars in a container with parchment between layers for up to 1 month.
variations: Use sliced strawberries instead of mixed berries.
Sprinkle with 2 tablespoons granola or chopped nuts before freezing.
Drizzle with 1 ounce melted dark chocolate after cutting.
Use blueberries, which are softer and less tart, and let the bar soften before eating.
Stir 1 scoop vanilla protein powder into the yogurt for about 3 g more protein per bar.
faq: Can I use nonfat yogurt?
Yes, but the bars freeze harder and icier. 2% gives a creamier bite.
Do I need to thaw them?
Just 5 minutes at room temperature.
Are they gluten-free?
Yes, as written.
note: A bar from the freezer is a small, cold treat with a little protein. Good on hot afternoons.

title: Creamy Split Pea Soup
subtitle: Split peas simmered in chicken bone broth with onion, carrot and celery, then blended smooth with a handful of spinach. About 15 g protein and 10 g fiber per small bowl.
desc: Smooth, filling and about 15 g protein.
intro: Split peas cook down into a naturally creamy soup without any cream. Simmered in chicken bone broth, each small bowl has about 15 g of protein and plenty of fiber, which makes it one of the most filling soups on the site for its size.
It is blended smooth, so it is easy to sip from a mug, and it freezes beautifully in single portions for harder days.

steps.d: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the split peas, broth, water and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover partly and simmer for 40 to 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until the peas are completely soft.
steps.tip: Split peas do not need soaking, but they do need stirring near the end so they do not stick.

steps.d: Remove the bay leaf. Stir in the spinach until wilted.
Blend with an immersion blender until smooth, adding a splash of water if it is too thick. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into small bowls or mugs.

tips: The soup thickens as it cools. Thin with water or broth when reheating.
Taste before salting; broth varies a lot.
A squeeze of lemon brightens it just before serving.
Small-portion tip: freeze in 1-cup containers so you only reheat what you need.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days or freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently, adding a little water.
variations: Stir in 1/2 cup diced lean ham after blending for about 3 g more protein per bowl.
Use vegetable broth; the protein drops to about 9 g per bowl.
Blend only half the soup for more texture.
Skip the bay leaf and pepper and serve warm rather than hot.
Swirl in 2 tablespoons Greek yogurt per bowl for about 3 g more protein.
faq: Do I need to soak split peas?
No. They soften in about 45 minutes of simmering.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, if your broth is gluten-free.
Can I use yellow split peas?
Yes; the soup will be golden instead of green, with the same nutrition.
note: A mug of this on a cold evening is about as comforting as food gets, and the split peas and bone broth bring about 15 g protein per bowl.

title: Chicken Minestrone with Small Pasta
subtitle: A light tomato-vegetable broth with tender chicken, white beans and a little small pasta. About 20 g protein per 1 1/2-cup bowl, and it freezes well.
desc: Vegetables, chicken and beans in every bowl.
intro: Classic minestrone is mostly vegetables and pasta. This version adds chicken and white beans, so each bowl has about 20 g of protein while still tasting like the soup you know.
The pasta is kept small and modest, and it makes a big pot that freezes well, so there is always a warm bowl ready.

steps.d: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook for 8 minutes, until softened. Add the zucchini and garlic and cook for 2 minutes more.
Add the tomatoes, broth and herbs, then lay the chicken breasts in the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook gently for 15 to 18 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
steps.tip: Poaching the chicken in the soup keeps it tender and flavors the broth.

steps.d: Lift out the chicken and shred it finely with two forks.
Add the pasta and beans to the pot and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, until the pasta is tender. Return the chicken and season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls and top each with a spoonful of parmesan and some fresh herbs.

tips: If freezing, cook the pasta separately and add it when reheating so it does not go soft.
Any small pasta works: ditalini, small shells or orzo.
A parmesan rind simmered in the broth adds lots of flavor.
Small-portion tip: a 1-cup bowl is plenty on low-appetite days.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days. Freeze without the pasta for up to 3 months; add freshly cooked pasta when reheating.
variations: Use leftover roast turkey instead of chicken.
Stir in a handful of chopped kale or spinach at the end.
Use a gluten-free small pasta or 1/2 cup rice.
Skip the garlic, shred the chicken very finely and serve warm.
Add an extra 1/2 can of white beans for about 2 g more protein per bowl.
faq: Can I use rotisserie chicken?
Yes. Skip the poaching step and add 3 cups shredded chicken with the beans.
Why is the pasta soft after a day?
Pasta keeps absorbing broth. Add a splash of broth when reheating, or cook pasta separately.
Is it dairy-free?
Yes, if you skip the parmesan.
note: A big pot of this on Sunday means warm, protein-rich bowls ready all week, one small portion at a time.

title: Smoky Chickpea and Black Bean Chili
subtitle: A thick, smoky vegetarian chili with chickpeas, black beans and tomatoes, topped with Greek yogurt. About 13 g protein and 13 g fiber per bowl.
desc: Thick, smoky and full of beans.
intro: This chili is built on two kinds of beans: chickpeas for a firm, nutty bite and black beans for creaminess. Smoked paprika and cumin give it a deep, smoky flavor without any meat.
A spoonful of Greek yogurt on top replaces sour cream and adds a little extra protein. It tastes even better the next day.
why: Two kinds of beans plus yogurt.

steps.d: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper for 6 to 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and spices and stir for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas, black beans, tomatoes and water. Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
steps.tip: Mash a few spoonfuls of beans against the side of the pot for a thicker chili.

steps.d: Taste and add salt, a pinch more chili or a squeeze of lime.
Ladle into bowls and top with a spoonful of Greek yogurt, cilantro and a few cucumber slices.

tips: Start with less chili powder; you can always add more.
Leftovers thicken overnight. Add a splash of water when reheating.
Serve over a little rice for a more filling meal.
Small-portion tip: 3/4 cup with a spoonful of yogurt is a satisfying small plate.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 5 days or freeze in portions for up to 3 months.
variations: Brown 1/2 lb lean ground turkey with the onion for about 8 g more protein per bowl.
Add 1 diced sweet potato with the tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes longer.
Top with avocado instead of yogurt.
Skip the chili powder and garlic and use sweet paprika instead of smoked.
Top with 2 tablespoons shredded cheese and extra yogurt for about 6 g more protein.
faq: Is it spicy?
Mildly. Adjust the chili powder to taste.
Can I use dried beans?
Yes, about 4 1/2 cups cooked beans in total.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, check that your spices and broth are gluten-free.
note: A pot of chili is one of the most forgiving things to cook. Make it once, and small bowls are ready all week.

title: Hearty Tomato White Bean Stew
subtitle: White beans and lean turkey sausage simmered in a smoky tomato broth. About 17 g protein per bowl, ready in 35 minutes.
desc: Beans and sausage in a smoky tomato broth.
intro: This stew sits between a soup and a chili: tender white beans and slices of lean turkey sausage in a thick, smoky tomato broth. It is warming, filling and has about 17 g of protein per bowl.
Serve a small bowl with a slice of bread for dipping, or on its own. It reheats and freezes well.

steps.d: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the sausage for 5 minutes, breaking it up if loose. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and paprika and cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans, broth and sausage. Simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
steps.tip: Mash some of the beans for a creamier stew.

steps.d: Season to taste and serve in small bowls with parsley.

tips: Check sausage labels; brands vary a lot in fat and salt.
A splash of vinegar or lemon at the end brightens the flavor.
Add a handful of spinach for color.
Small-portion tip: serve 3/4 cup with a small piece of bread for dipping.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days or freeze for up to 3 months.
variations: Use chicken sausage instead of turkey.
Skip the sausage and add a third can of beans.
Stir in chopped kale for the last 5 minutes.
Use a mild sausage, skip the paprika and garlic, and mash most of the beans.
Top with grated parmesan for about 3 g more protein.
faq: What beans work best?
Cannellini or great northern beans.
Is it gluten-free?
Check your sausage and broth labels.
Can I make it in a slow cooker?
Yes. Brown the sausage, then cook everything on low for 6 hours.
note: This is cozy, simple food: a small bowl of beans in tomato broth, a little bread, and you are done.

title: Turkish-Style Red Lentil Soup with Lemon
subtitle: Red lentils simmered in bone broth with onion, cumin and paprika, blended silky smooth and finished with lemon and mint. About 14 g protein per small bowl.
desc: Silky, lemony and very easy to sip.
intro: Red lentils fall apart as they cook, so this soup blends into something silky and smooth with no cream at all. It is inspired by Turkish mercimek çorbası: gently spiced with cumin and paprika and finished with a squeeze of lemon.
Using bone broth adds protein, giving each small bowl about 14 g. It is a mild, soothing soup that is easy to sip from a mug.

steps.d: Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 6 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, cumin and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, broth and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered for 20 to 25 minutes, until the lentils have completely broken down.
Blend until silky smooth. Add water if it is too thick.
steps.tip: Blend a little longer than you think for the silkiest texture.

steps.d: Stir in most of the lemon juice and season with salt. Serve with a sprinkle of dried mint and a little more lemon.

tips: Add lemon at the end, to taste; it lifts the whole soup.
The soup thickens as it sits. Thin with water when reheating.
A drizzle of olive oil warmed with paprika is a traditional topping.
Small-portion tip: serve it in a mug and sip it slowly.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days or freeze in portions for up to 3 months.
variations: Use vegetable broth; the protein drops to about 9 g per bowl.
Add 2 tablespoons fine bulgur with the lentils for a more traditional texture.
Top with a teaspoon of butter melted with paprika.
Skip the paprika and use just a little lemon.
Swirl 2 tablespoons Greek yogurt into each bowl for about 3 g more protein.
faq: Do red lentils need soaking?
No. They cook in about 20 minutes.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, if your broth is gluten-free and you skip the bulgur.
Can I use green lentils?
They hold their shape and take longer; the soup will not be as smooth.
note: This is a gentle, golden soup for slow days. A squeeze of lemon at the end makes it taste bright and fresh.

title: Chicken and Zucchini Stir-Fry
subtitle: Tender strips of chicken and zucchini in a light garlic-ginger soy glaze, ready in 25 minutes. About 28 g protein per small plate.
desc: Quick, light and about 28 g protein.
intro: A stir-fry is one of the fastest ways to get a warm, protein-rich plate on the table. Thin strips of chicken breast cook in minutes, and zucchini adds volume without making the plate heavy. Each small plate has about 28 g of protein.

The glaze is simple: low-sodium soy sauce, a little honey, garlic and ginger, thickened with a spoonful of cornstarch so it clings instead of pooling. Serve it on its own or over a small scoop of rice.
why: Clings to the chicken without a heavy sauce.

steps.d: Toss the chicken strips with the cornstarch until lightly coated. Stir the soy sauce, honey and water together in a small bowl.

Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in a single layer and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through to 165°F (74°C). Move to a plate.
steps.tip: Cook in two batches if your pan is small, so the chicken browns instead of steaming.

steps.d: Add the onion, pepper and zucchini to the pan and stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes, until just tender. Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce and toss for 1 to 2 minutes, until glossy and slightly thickened.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve on small plates, with a little rice if you like.

tips: Slice the chicken thin and even so it cooks fast and stays tender.
Do not overcook the zucchini; it should still have a little bite.
Swap the honey for a pinch of sugar if you prefer.
Small-portion tip: serve a small plate with more chicken than vegetables, and keep the rest for lunch tomorrow.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a skillet with a splash of water, or in the microwave.
variations: Use small broccoli florets instead of the pepper.
Use tamari instead of soy sauce.
Use peeled shrimp and cook them for just 2 to 3 minutes.
Skip the garlic and ginger, and peel the zucchini for a softer texture.
Add 1 cup shelled edamame with the vegetables for about 4 g more protein per plate.
faq: Can I use chicken thighs?
Yes. Boneless thighs stay juicier; cook them to 175°F (80°C).
Does the nutrition include rice?
No. A 1/3-cup scoop of cooked rice adds about 70 kcal.
Is it dairy-free?
Yes.
note: This is a weeknight plate that comes together faster than takeout, in a portion that is easy to finish.

title: Lemon Herb Baked Cod with Rice
subtitle: Mild, flaky cod baked with olive oil, lemon, garlic and herbs, served with a small scoop of rice. About 22 g protein per plate, ready in 20 minutes.
desc: Mild, flaky and very easy to eat.
intro: Cod is one of the gentlest proteins you can cook: mild in flavor, soft in texture and quick to bake. A drizzle of olive oil, lemon and herbs is all it needs, and each 4-ounce piece has about 20 g of protein.
Serve it with a small scoop of rice and a squeeze of lemon. Any firm white fish works the same way, including haddock, pollock or tilapia.
why: From a 4-ounce piece of cod plus rice.
Mild flavor and soft, flaky texture.

steps.d: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and lightly oil a baking dish.
Pat the cod dry and place it in the dish. Mix the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, herbs and paprika, then spoon it over the fish. Season with salt and pepper and lay a lemon slice on each piece.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the fish flakes easily and reaches 145°F (63°C).
steps.tip: Thin fillets cook faster; start checking at 10 minutes.

steps.d: Serve each piece with a small scoop of rice, spoon over the pan juices and finish with fresh herbs.

tips: Frozen cod works; thaw it overnight in the fridge and pat it very dry.
Spoon the pan juices over the rice for extra flavor.
A few cherry tomatoes in the dish make a quick side.
Small-portion tip: start with half a fillet and a spoonful of rice.
storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat gently, covered, in a low oven, or flake cold over a salad.
variations: Serve with small boiled potatoes instead of rice.
Sprinkle 2 tablespoons panko over the fish before baking.
Skip the garlic and paprika and serve with plain rice.
Serve with a spoonful of Greek yogurt mixed with dill and lemon for about 3 g more protein.
faq: How do I know it is done?
The fish turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork, at 145°F (63°C).
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, as written.
Can I skip the rice?
Yes. The fish alone is about 125 kcal and 20 g protein.
note: This is a calm, simple plate for evenings when you want something warm and light that still does real work.

title: Turkey and Rice Stuffed Peppers
subtitle: Small green peppers filled with lean ground turkey, rice, herbs and tomato, baked until tender and finished with Greek yogurt. About 19 g protein per pepper.
desc: One pepper is one small plate.
intro: Stuffed peppers portion themselves: one pepper is one small plate. This filling is lean ground turkey with a modest amount of rice, onion, herbs and tomato, so each pepper has about 19 g of protein.
The peppers bake in a little tomato sauce until soft, and a spoonful of Greek yogurt on top keeps them cool and creamy. They reheat well, so a batch covers several meals.
why: Lean turkey plus a yogurt topping.

steps.d: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Stand the peppers upright in a baking dish that holds them snugly.
Warm the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, add the garlic, then the turkey. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in the rice, half the tomato sauce, the herbs and salt.

Spoon the filling into the peppers. Pour the remaining sauce and 1/4 cup water around them. Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 minutes more, until the peppers are tender.
steps.tip: For softer peppers, microwave them for 3 minutes before stuffing.

steps.d: Top each pepper with a spoonful of Greek yogurt and a little extra dill.

tips: Choose small peppers that stand upright; they make better single portions.
Red or yellow peppers are sweeter and softer than green.
Leftover rice works perfectly in the filling.
Small-portion tip: start with half a pepper (about 10 g protein) and a spoonful of yogurt.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days. Freeze cooked peppers individually for up to 3 months and reheat covered in the oven or microwave.
variations: Use ground chicken instead of turkey.
Replace half the turkey with cooked lentils.
Add 1 tablespoon shredded mozzarella per pepper for the last 10 minutes.
Use red peppers, skip the garlic and bake until very soft.
Add 1/2 cup cottage cheese to the filling for about 2 g more protein per pepper.
faq: Do I need to precook the peppers?
No, but a quick microwave makes them softer.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, if your tomato sauce is gluten-free.
Can I make them ahead?
Yes. Stuff them, refrigerate up to a day, then bake.
note: A tray of these in the fridge means a warm, ready portion every time you open it.

title: Creamy Garlic Shrimp with Zucchini Noodles
subtitle: Shrimp and zucchini noodles in a light creamy sauce made with Greek yogurt and Parmesan. About 29 g protein per small plate, ready in 20 minutes.
desc: Creamy, garlicky and very light.
intro: Zucchini noodles make a light base, and shrimp cook in just a few minutes, so this plate is fast and easy on a small appetite. Each portion has about 29 g of protein.
The creamy sauce is Greek yogurt and Parmesan stirred in off the heat, which keeps it smooth without any cream. Squeeze over lemon and finish with fresh herbs.
why: Greek yogurt makes the sauce creamy.

steps.d: Pat the shrimp dry and season lightly. Warm the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until pink. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the zucchini noodles. Toss for 2 to 3 minutes, just until warm.
steps.tip: Do not overcook the zucchini noodles or they release water and turn soft.

steps.t: Make the sauce off the heat
steps.d: Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the yogurt, Parmesan and lemon juice until creamy, then return the shrimp and toss.
steps.tip: Adding yogurt off the heat keeps it from splitting.

steps.d: Divide among small plates and finish with parsley and a pinch of chili flakes.

tips: Pat the zucchini noodles dry with a towel before cooking.
Frozen shrimp work well; thaw them in cold water and dry well.
Store-bought zucchini noodles save time.
Small-portion tip: five or six shrimp with a small nest of noodles is a satisfying small plate.
storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 1 day and reheat gently; the noodles will soften.
variations: Mix the zucchini noodles with 2 oz cooked spaghetti for a heartier plate.
Use thin chicken strips, cooked through to 165°F (74°C).
Use a dairy-free yogurt and skip the Parmesan.
Use 1 garlic clove, skip the chili flakes and serve warm.
Add 2 tablespoons more Parmesan for about 4 g more protein.
faq: Why did my sauce split?
The pan was too hot. Stir the yogurt in off the heat.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, as written.
Can I use pasta instead?
Yes. Use about 6 oz pasta; the calories and carbs will go up.
note: Light, quick and creamy: a plate that feels like a treat without being heavy.

title: Greek Yogurt Egg Salad Lettuce Wraps
subtitle: Creamy egg salad made with Greek yogurt and a little light mayo, spooned into butter lettuce cups and served with a few crackers. About 17 g protein per serving.
desc: Soft, cool and easy to eat.
intro: Egg salad is soft, cool and mild, which makes it a good fit for days when hot food does not sound good. This version uses mostly Greek yogurt with just a little light mayo, so it stays creamy and adds protein. Each serving has about 17 g.
Spoon it into butter lettuce leaves for a light wrap, with a few whole-grain crackers on the side for crunch. The egg salad keeps for a few days in the fridge.

items.n: salt, pepper and a squeeze of lemon

steps.d: Place the eggs in a pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat, cover and let stand for 11 minutes.
Move the eggs to a bowl of ice water for 5 minutes, then peel.
steps.tip: Peeling under running water makes it easier.

steps.d: Chop the eggs and stir with the yogurt, mayo, Dijon, celery and herbs. Season with salt, pepper and a squeeze of lemon.
Spoon the egg salad into the lettuce leaves and serve with crackers on the side.

tips: Mash the eggs finely for a softer, smoother egg salad.
Chill the egg salad for 20 minutes for the best flavor.
Keep the lettuce and egg salad separate until serving.
Small-portion tip: one wrap and two crackers make a light small plate.
storage: Refrigerate the egg salad in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Fill the lettuce just before eating.
variations: Replace the mayo with 1/4 mashed avocado.
Serve on a small slice of whole-grain toast instead of lettuce.
Skip the mustard and celery and mash the eggs smooth.
Add 2 tablespoons more Greek yogurt and serve with an extra egg white for about 5 g more protein.
faq: Can I make it without mayo?
Yes. Use all Greek yogurt and a little extra Dijon.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, with gluten-free crackers or none.
How long does it keep?
Up to 3 days in the fridge.
note: A cool, soft plate for warm days or slow afternoons, ready in the fridge whenever you need it.

title: Gentle Chicken Rice Congee with Soft Egg
subtitle: Rice simmered slowly in chicken bone broth until soft and porridge-like, with finely shredded chicken, ginger and half a soft-boiled egg. About 23 g protein per small bowl.
desc: Soft, warm and about 23 g protein.
intro: Congee is rice cooked in plenty of broth until the grains break down into a soft, silky porridge. It is one of the gentlest warm foods there is: mild, smooth and easy to eat a few spoonfuls at a time.
Cooking the rice in chicken bone broth and stirring in finely shredded chicken gives each small bowl about 23 g of protein. Half a soft-boiled egg, a little ginger and green onion finish it.

steps.d: Put the rice, broth, water and ginger in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer partly covered for 45 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until the rice has broken down into a thick porridge.
steps.tip: Stir more often near the end so the rice does not stick.

steps.d: After 20 minutes, add the whole chicken breast to the pot and simmer for 15 to 18 minutes, until it reaches 165°F (74°C). Lift it out.
Shred the chicken very finely with two forks and stir it back into the congee. Remove the ginger and season with a little salt.
Lower the eggs into simmering water for 7 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Ladle into small bowls and top each with half an egg, green onion, a few drops of sesame oil and soy sauce.

tips: Add hot water when reheating; congee thickens a lot as it cools.
For a smoother texture, blend a ladleful and stir it back in.
A slow cooker works too: 6 hours on low.
Small-portion tip: start with a smaller bowl topped with half an egg. It is soft and easy to eat in small spoonfuls; add the other half of the egg if you want more.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days. Freeze without the eggs for up to 3 months and reheat with a splash of water.
variations: Stir in small pieces of white fish for the last 5 minutes instead of chicken.
Use vegetable broth and silken tofu; the protein drops to about 9 g per bowl.
Use brown rice and simmer 20 minutes longer.
Skip the ginger, sesame oil and soy sauce and serve warm, not hot.
Top with a whole egg instead of half for about 3 g more protein.
faq: Why so much liquid?
Congee needs about 14 parts liquid to 1 part rice to become soft and porridge-like.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, with tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce and broth.
Can I use leftover rice?
Yes. Simmer 1 1/2 cups cooked rice in the broth for about 25 minutes.
note: Congee is what many people reach for when they feel unwell, and for good reason. It is warm, soft and easy, and this version adds finely shredded chicken and a soft egg.

title: Creamy Cottage Cheese Mashed Potatoes
subtitle: Soft Yukon Gold potatoes mashed with blended cottage cheese, a little Greek yogurt and butter, topped with green onion. About 12 g protein per small bowl.
desc: Soft, creamy mash with a protein lift.
intro: Mashed potatoes are one of the softest, most comforting foods there is. Blending cottage cheese until smooth and folding it in keeps them creamy and adds protein, so each small bowl has about 12 g instead of the usual 4.
Eat a small bowl on its own on hard days, or serve it next to a little salmon, chicken or turkey meatballs for a fuller plate.
why: Easy to eat in small spoonfuls.

steps.d: Cover the potatoes with cold salted water, bring to a boil and simmer for 15 to 18 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
While they cook, blend the cottage cheese and yogurt until completely smooth.
steps.tip: Blending removes the curds, so the mash stays silky.

steps.d: Drain the potatoes well and return them to the warm pot. Mash with the butter, then stir in the blended cottage cheese and enough warm milk for a soft texture.
Season with salt and pepper and serve in small bowls, topped with green onion.

tips: Yukon Golds make the creamiest mash; russets are fluffier.
Keep the heat off once the dairy goes in so it stays smooth.
Reheat with a splash of milk.
Small-portion tip: serve a 1/2-cup scoop on its own, or next to a few bites of salmon, chicken or turkey meatballs.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days. Reheat gently in a covered pot or the microwave with a little milk.
variations: Simmer 2 peeled garlic cloves with the potatoes and mash them in.
Replace half the potatoes with cauliflower florets.
Skip the pepper and green onion and keep the mash extra smooth.
Top with a soft egg or serve with shredded chicken for 6 to 10 g more protein.
faq: Can I taste the cottage cheese?
Barely. Blended smooth, it tastes like a creamy, slightly tangy mash.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, as written.
Can I freeze it?
Yes, for up to 2 months; stir well when reheating.
note: A warm bowl of mashed potatoes asks very little of a small appetite, and blending in cottage cheese gives this one about three times the protein of a plain mash.

title: Savory Herbed Cottage Cheese Bowl
subtitle: Cool cottage cheese with green onion, cucumber, cherry tomatoes, a drizzle of olive oil and everything seasoning. No cooking, about 25 g protein per bowl.
desc: Five minutes, no cooking, about 25 g protein.
intro: Cottage cheese is one of the easiest high-protein foods to keep in the fridge, and it does not have to be sweet. Topped with green onion, cucumber and tomatoes, it becomes a cool, savory bowl in five minutes.
Each bowl has about 25 g of protein, and it needs no cooking at all, which makes it a good option for warm days or tired evenings.
why: Easy when hot food does not appeal.

steps.d: Spoon the cottage cheese into two bowls.
Scatter over the green onion, cucumber and tomatoes.
Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with seasoning and herbs. Serve cold.

tips: Small-curd cottage cheese feels softer and smoother.
Blend the cottage cheese first if you do not like the curds.
Add a few whole-grain crackers for crunch.
Small-portion tip: half a bowl is still about 12 g protein.
storage: Best fresh. Cottage cheese keeps in the fridge until its date once opened; add the vegetables just before eating.
variations: Top with olives, a little feta and oregano.
Add a few slices of avocado.
Spread on a small slice of whole-grain toast.
Skip the onion and seasoning and top with peeled cucumber only.
Add a chopped hard-boiled egg for about 6 g more protein.
faq: Is cottage cheese salty?
It can be. Low-sodium versions are available; skip the seasoning if using regular.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, if your seasoning is gluten-free.
Can I make it ahead?
Keep the vegetables chopped in a separate container and assemble when ready.
note: This is the bowl to make when you know you need protein and cannot face cooking.

title: Blueberry Greek Yogurt Chia Pudding
subtitle: Chia seeds soaked overnight in milk and Greek yogurt, topped with blueberries and almond flakes. Soft, cool and about 13 g protein per jar.
desc: Make it tonight, eat it cold tomorrow.
intro: Chia seeds soak up liquid and turn into a soft, spoonable pudding with no cooking. Mixing in Greek yogurt makes it creamier and adds protein, so each small jar has about 13 g.
It needs a few hours in the fridge, so it is ideal to make in the evening. Top with blueberries and a few almond flakes before eating.

steps.d: Whisk the milk, yogurt, maple syrup and vanilla until smooth, then whisk in the chia seeds.
Wait 5 minutes and whisk again to break up any clumps.
steps.tip: This second stir is what keeps the pudding smooth.

steps.d: Divide among three small jars, cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Stir, then top with blueberries and almonds.

tips: For a completely smooth texture, blend the pudding after it sets.
Add a splash of milk if it is too thick.
Frozen blueberries work; thaw them first.
Small-portion tip: start with a few spoonfuls on hard days; the rest keeps in the fridge.
storage: Refrigerate in covered jars for up to 4 days. Add toppings just before eating.
variations: Top with diced mango instead of blueberries.
Use soy milk and a thick plant yogurt; protein will be lower.
Blend it smooth and skip the almonds.
Whisk in 1 scoop vanilla protein powder with extra milk for about 7 g more protein per jar.
faq: Why is my pudding lumpy?
Whisk again after 5 minutes; the seeds clump at first.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, as written.
Can I skip the yogurt?
Yes, use 2 cups milk total, but the protein drops to about 6 g.
note: A jar waiting in the fridge makes the first meal of a hard day one less decision.

title: Creamy Protein Rice Pudding with Berries
subtitle: Arborio rice cooked slowly in ultra-filtered milk with vanilla and cinnamon, served warm or cold with fresh berries. About 11 g protein per small bowl.
desc: Soft, creamy and comforting, warm or cold.
intro: Rice pudding is soft, mild and comforting, and it is good warm or straight from the fridge. Cooking it in ultra-filtered milk, which has more protein than regular milk, gives each small bowl about 11 g.
A little maple syrup, vanilla and cinnamon keep it lightly sweet, and fresh berries add brightness on top.
why: Easy to eat a few spoonfuls.

steps.d: Put the rice, milk and salt in a heavy saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring.
Lower the heat and cook uncovered for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is very soft and the pudding is thick and creamy.
steps.tip: Keep the heat low; milk scorches easily.

steps.d: Stir in the maple syrup, vanilla and cinnamon.
Serve warm, or chill for a thicker pudding. Top with berries.

tips: The pudding thickens a lot as it cools; stir in a splash of milk to loosen.
Regular milk works, but the protein drops to about 7 g per bowl.
A strip of lemon zest in the milk adds a fresh note.
Small-portion tip: a 1/2-cup bowl is a satisfying small dessert.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days. Eat cold or rewarm with a little milk.
variations: Use half coconut milk; protein will be lower.
Add a pinch of ground cardamom with the cinnamon.
Top with soft cooked apple instead of berries.
Skip the cinnamon and serve with blueberries, which are less tart.
Stir 1/2 cup Greek yogurt into the cooled pudding for about 3 g more protein per bowl.
faq: What is ultra-filtered milk?
Milk filtered to concentrate the protein; check labels, as values vary by brand.
Is it gluten-free?
Yes, as written.
Can I use leftover rice?
Yes. Simmer 1 cup cooked rice in 2 cups milk for about 15 minutes.
note: Soft, sweet and familiar, this is a small dessert that is easy to say yes to.
